# Tumor-Infiltrating Stromal Reaction in Histology

## Definition
The **stromal reaction** (also called desmoplastic reaction or tumor stroma) refers to the host tissue response surrounding and infiltrating a tumor, consisting of non-neoplastic cells and extracellular matrix.

## Key Components

### Cellular Elements
- **Fibroblasts/Myofibroblasts** (cancer-associated fibroblasts - CAFs)
- **Immune cells** (lymphocytes, macrophages, neutrophils)
- **Endothelial cells** (new blood vessels)
- **Pericytes**

### Extracellular Matrix
- Collagen (types I, III)
- Fibronectin
- Hyaluronic acid
- Proteoglycans

## Histological Appearance

| Feature | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Desmoplasia** | Dense fibrous tissue surrounding tumor nests |
| **Inflammatory infiltrate** | Variable lymphocytic/myeloid cell presence |
| **Neovascularization** | New, often abnormal blood vessels |
| **Myxoid change** | Loose, edematous stroma |

## Clinical Significance

- **Prognostic value**: Lymphocyte-rich stroma often indicates better prognosis
- **Tumor behavior**: Desmoplastic reaction can indicate invasiveness
- **Treatment response**: May predict response to immunotherapy
- **Grading systems**: Some cancers (breast, colon) incorporate stromal features

## Examples
- Breast carcinoma (prominent desmoplasia)
- Pancreatic adenocarcinoma (dense stroma)
- Colorectal cancer (Klintrup-Mäkinen grade)
